transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi… thanks for seeing me. I guess it’s about flying. It’s probably not a huge deal compared to what other people come in for, but it’s started feeling a lot scarier than I think it should. Even just thinking about getting on a plane, I kind of picture this really bad turbulence we had on my honeymoon flight. I know planes are safe and people fly all the time, so I feel a little silly saying it, but it’s been bothering me.
Have you been avoiding flying or putting off trips that involve flying because of these scary feelings?

Yeah… a little. I mean, I try not to make a big deal of it, but I have been choosing to drive really long distances instead of flying. And I’ve turned down a couple work trainings if they meant getting on a plane.

If I absolutely have to talk through a trip, I kind of need my husband sitting with me, or I start feeling like I’m going to back out. I know that probably sounds dramatic… but that’s how it’s been.
Have you ever had a panic attack while on a plane?

I don’t know if I’d call it a full panic attack, exactly… I mean, I don’t want to overstate it. But even when I’m just looking at flights for a conference, or if I hear a plane overhead, my chest tightens right away and I get this rush of panic, like I need to close the laptop or get away from the thought. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you experience this kind of panic or anxiety in situations other than when you're thinking about or are on a plane?

Um… I don’t think so, not really. I mean, I get normal stress like anyone, but that sudden panicky feeling seems tied to planes or thinking about flying. I haven’t really noticed it happening in other situations. Is that… does that make sense?
How long have you been experiencing this anxiety related to flying?

I guess it’s been a little over two years… about two years and five months, really. It started after this really turbulent flight coming back from my honeymoon. I kept thinking it would just fade, so I didn’t make much of it at first, but it’s kind of stuck around since then.
Have you avoided any other activities or situations because of your fear of flying?

A little, yeah… I mean, I try not to make it a big thing. But I’ve chosen really long drives instead, or I’ve turned down a couple of work trainings if flying was involved. And if I absolutely have to talk through a trip, I usually need my husband sitting with me, just so I don’t back out. Is that the kind of avoidance you mean?
Has your fear of flying affected your relationships with family or friends in any way?

A little, I guess. I mean, I’m still doing okay day to day — work and home are fine, mostly. But it has made some things harder. I’ve passed up a few trainings or conferences my supervisor thought would be good for me, which I feel kind of embarrassed about.

And personally, it’s pushed back plans too… like there was this Florence trip I was really excited about, and I keep finding reasons to delay it. So it’s not ruining my relationships or anything, but I know it probably affects plans with people more than I want to admit. Does that answer what you mean?
Can you describe what happens physically when you start feeling anxious about flying, like with the chest tightening you mentioned?

Yeah… it’s usually pretty immediate. Like if I’m just looking at flights for a conference, or even sometimes if I hear a plane going overhead, my chest kind of tightens right away.

I know that probably sounds a little dramatic, but it’s like this quick rush of panic, and my first instinct is to shut the laptop or just get away from the thought completely. Is that what you mean?
Is there anything else that triggers this kind of panic or anxiety for you, besides flying or thoughts of flying?

Not really, no… at least nothing that comes to mind the same way. It’s pretty much tied to flying or things that make me think about flying. I mean, I get normal stress like anyone, but not that sudden panic feeling. Does that make sense?
Do you feel like your fear of flying is controlling your life or causing you a lot of distress?

I wouldn’t say it’s controlling my whole life, exactly… I mean, I’m still getting to work, taking care of things at home, all of that is okay.

But it does bother me more than I probably like to admit. I’ve started turning down or avoiding trainings and conferences my supervisor thinks would be good for me, and I feel kind of bad about that. And personally, it keeps pushing back things too, like this Florence trip I was really excited about.

So… not controlling everything, but it is getting in the way. Is that a fair way to put it?
Are there any hobbies or personal interests that you've had to give up or reduce because of your fear of flying?

I don’t think I’ve fully given up hobbies, exactly… I’m still doing my usual day-to-day stuff, and home and work are mostly okay.

But I guess it has reduced some personal things I wanted to do. Like I keep putting off that Florence trip I was really excited about, because getting there would mean flying. And work-wise, I’ve passed on some trainings and conferences my supervisor thought would be good for me. So… maybe not hobbies in the strict sense, but it is limiting things I care about. Does that answer it?
Have you ever avoided a significant life event or opportunity solely because it required flying?

I guess… yes, a little. I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is, but I have chosen long drives instead of flying, and I’ve turned down some work trainings because getting there would mean a flight.

And if I absolutely have to talk through a trip that involves flying, I usually need my husband sitting with me, or I start backing out of it in my head. I know that probably counts, right?
Has your fear of flying caused any problems in your daily routine or relationships that you feel are significant?

Not in a huge way, I don’t think… like, I’m still getting through my normal job and home responsibilities. My relationships aren’t falling apart or anything like that.

But it does create problems around plans. I’ve been passing up trainings and conferences my supervisor thinks would help me grow, and I feel awkward about that. And personally, it keeps delaying things I was excited about, like the Florence trip. So… significant maybe in those areas, but I don’t want to overstate it.
Are there any social events or leisure activities that you've stopped doing or reduced because of your fear of flying?

A little, yes… I wouldn’t say I’ve stopped having a social life or anything. I’m still managing work and home pretty normally.

But I have reduced things that would involve traveling by plane. Like I keep pushing back the Florence trip I was excited about, and I’ve passed up some trainings and conferences my supervisor thought would be good for me. So it’s not every leisure activity, but when flying is involved, I tend to avoid it or put it off. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
